business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Shanti Inorganics Limited manufactures and trades sulphur based inorganic chemicals, with a product portfolio of ammonium bisulphite, sodium bisulphite solutions, sodium meta/bisulphite and sodium sulphite powder. These are used as preservatives, reducing agents, oxygen scavengers and process intermediates across oil drilling, pharmaceuticals, food and beverages, pulp & paper and water treatment. Products are supplied in two grades, food grade and technical grade, to customers in India and in export markets including Azerbaijan, Colombia, Egypt, Eswatini, Iraq, Turkey, Malaysia, Nigeria, Puerto Rico, Qatar, Russia, UAE, Oman and Vietnam.

group_structure.body:

- Jagjanani Textiles Limited — Other venture / other directorship of Promoter Avnish Manojkumar Patel: Avnish Manojkumar Patel is Managing Director and Member; it is his only other Indian directorship

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Backward-integration steps and in-process recycling are described; the DRHP does not claim end-to-end integration. (1) Input-route change: "In Fiscal 2019, we transitioned from using sulphur burning furnaces to procuring liquefied sulphur dioxide (SO2) which improved production efficiency, reduced emissions and enhanced environmental compliance" – a move AWAY from in-house SO2 generation toward bought-in SO2. (2) Proposed re-integration at Manufacturing Unit – II Phase II: turnkey plant and machinery includes "a sulphur burner system, ammonium bisulphite system and Sodium metabisulphite (SMBS) system engineering and equipment"; "The use of sulphur burner technology will allow us to produce steam without relying on any external fuel sources that will significantly reduce energy costs. The waste heat boiler will generate fuel-free steam, which will be utilized across various plant operations" – energy self-generation from the process itself. (3) Locational integration: units are sited close to industries that generate liquefied SO2, securing liquid SO2, sodium carbonate, sodium hydroxide and liquid ammonia and reducing logistics cost and lead time; long-term relationships with key suppliers are stated. (4) In-process recycling: in the sodium metabisulphite route the soda ash / caustic soda slurry is mixed with "a recycled solution called mother liquor, which helps to reduce waste and reuse materials", the leftover liquid after centrifuging is recycled back into the process, and the separated crystals are dried using waste steam; in the ammonium bisulphite route "a water scrubber system is attached to trap any leftover ammonia fumes, and these captured gases are recycled back into the process to avoid waste". (5) Forward integration: none disclosed – sales are direct business-to-business to end-use customers through the Company's own sales team, with no owned distribution, warehousing or downstream processing described.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Disruption in supply of raw materials and cost of raw materials
- Increasing competition in the chemical industry
- Dependence on end customers
- Ability to maintain cordial relationships with customers and suppliers
- Ability to successfully implement the growth expansion plan
- Optimum capacity utilisation of the installed capacity
- Changes in Government regulations, tax regime, laws and other regulations applicable to the industry
- Geopolitical and global trade conditions
- Fluctuation in foreign currency rates
- Financial statements are prepared under Indian GAAP, not Ind AS / IFRS / U.S. GAAP, with no reconciliation provided

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Set up Phase II of the Bavla Unit (Manufacturing Unit - II) at Plot No. 6 and 7, Sankalp Industrial Estate, Moje Chidaya, Bavla, with a proposed installed capacity of 31,200 MTPA of sodium metabisulphite, sodium bisulphite and ammonium bisulphite in both food and technical grades, part funded from the Net Proceeds
- Continue expanding production and operational capabilities as done since incorporation (liquid and powder sodium bisulphite, sodium metabisulphite, ammonium bisulphite solutions in Fiscal 2016, capacity expansion from 10,700 MTPA to 16,200 MTPA in Fiscal 2022)
- Leverage proximity to raw material sources and long-term supplier relationships to offer competitive pricing while meeting growing demand
- Use the listing of Equity Shares to enhance visibility and brand image among existing and potential customers

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company operates an existing 18,800 MTPA unit at Vatva, Ahmedabad, and acquired land at Bavla, Ahmedabad for Manufacturing Unit - II to be built in two phases. Phase I (Plot no. 5/A & 5/B, Sankalp Industrial Estate, Village Chiyada, Bavla; 8,601.10 sq m) commenced commercial production with effect from February 2025 with an installed capacity of 18,000 MTPA. The upcoming Phase II at Plot No. 6 and 7, Sankalp Industrial Estate, Moje Chidaya, Bavla (~17,212.07 sq m) is proposed to have an installed capacity of 31,200 MTPA to manufacture sodium metabisulphite, sodium bisulphite and ammonium bisulphite in all grades, food and technical. This new facility is the "Proposed Project" for which the Issue proceeds are being raised, with ₹4,300.00 lakhs of Net Proceeds earmarked as part funding of the capital expenditure. Earlier expansions include the Fiscal 2019 shift from sulphur burning furnaces to procuring liquefied sulphur dioxide (SO2), which improved production efficiency and reduced emissions, and the Fiscal 2022 capacity expansion from 10,700 MTPA to 16,200 MTPA through new plant and equipment (dryers, centrifuges, storage tanks and heat exchangers).

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Geographical diversification through exports - export sales were 53.83%, 50.08% and 52.59% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023, across Azerbaijan, Colombia, Egypt, Eswatini, Iraq, Turkey, Malaysia, Nigeria, Puerto Rico, Qatar, Russia, UAE, Oman and Vietnam
- Long standing relationships with a diversified customer base across multiple industries - 51/47/43 domestic and 21/21/15 international customers in Fiscals 2025/2024/2023; 4 of the top 10 Fiscal 2025 customers associated for more than five years
- Strategically located production facilities close to industries generating liquefied sulphur dioxide (SO2), giving reliable access to key raw materials (liquid SO2, sodium carbonate, sodium hydroxide, liquid ammonia), reduced logistics costs and lead times, and long-term supplier relationships
- Certifications and compliance with quality and food safety standards - ISO 9001:2015, NSF, KOSHER, HACCP and HALAL, widening access to food & beverage, potable water and international markets
- Experienced Promoters and senior management with extensive domain knowledge in sulphur based inorganic chemicals, actively involved in production, administration, business development and finance

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- End-industry concentration in food & beverages, oil-field and chemicals — Risk Factor 1: these three industries together accounted for more than 75% of revenue in each of the last three fiscal years (F&B 40.84%/37.75%/37.91%, oil-field 19.55%/14.41%/17.25%, chemicals 15.76%/16.62%/16.76% in Fiscals 2025/2024/2023); any material decline in their performance may adversely affect operations and results
- Customer concentration — Top 10 customers contributed 68.14%, 67.41% and 73.58% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023, and the single largest customer 15.10%, 11.33% and 12.88%; loss of a few customers would be material
- Export dependence and foreign currency exposure — Export sales were 53.83%, 50.08% and 52.59% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023 across 14 named countries; the MD&A lists geopolitical and global trade conditions and fluctuation in foreign currency rates as significant factors affecting results
- Raw material supply and price risk — Production depends on liquefied sulphur dioxide (SO2), sodium carbonate, sodium hydroxide and liquid ammonia sourced from nearby generating industries; the MD&A names disruption in supply and cost of raw materials as a significant factor affecting results
- Execution and utilisation risk on the two-phase Bavla expansion — Bavla Phase I only commenced commercial production in February 2025 and Phase II (31,200 MTPA) is yet to be built and is part funded by the Issue; the MD&A names the ability to successfully implement the growth expansion plan and optimum capacity utilisation of installed capacity as significant factors
- Leverage rose alongside the capex programme — Total debt rose from ₹562.52 lakhs in Fiscal 2023 to ₹2,434.05 lakhs in Fiscal 2024 and ₹2,538.03 lakhs in Fiscal 2025, with debt to equity of 0.45, 1.38 and 0.98 respectively; ROCE fell from 49.34% in Fiscal 2023 to 27.59% and 27.20%
- Competition in the chemical industry — Increasing competition in the chemical industry is listed in the MD&A as a significant factor affecting the Company's results of operations
- Reliance on a commissioned industry report — Industry and market information is derived from the "Industry Research Report on Inorganic Chemicals Industry" dated September 19, 2025 by CARE, commissioned and paid for by the Company exclusively for the Issue and not independently verified by the Company, the BRLM or any other person connected with the Issue
